subject: Pilot pricing & efficiency roadmap — quantization, batching, and KV-cache guardrails
messages:
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@fastops.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot inquiry — efficiency + pricing questions

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the call this morning. BlueHarbor is excited to run a 6-week pilot to validate token-cost improvements for our chat summarization workflow. A few discrete asks we want to lock down before legal:

- Pilot scope (throughput targets, typical seq-lengths) — we attached our sample request traces.
- A short list of recommended model/quantization combos.
- How batching and prefix/KV cache will be measured (we need a conservative estimate for expected per-token savings).
- A simple pricing construct for the pilot (credits, cap on spend, fallback behavior if we exceed burst capacity).

Can you share the pilot scope doc and a pricing sketch we can circulate with procurement? Also looping procurement on this message.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Lee | Director, AI Platforms | FastOps
Attachments: sample_requests.ndjson (attachment stub, 2.3MB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@fastops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@blueharbor.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot inquiry — efficiency + pricing questions

Hi Sam — great to speak earlier. Quick summary and what I’m attaching:

1) Pilot scope (attached: pilot_scope_v2.pdf) — targets: 100 concurrent users, median seq 320 toks, 95p latency < 350ms for short-turn queries.
2) Recommended stack: Llama-3-70B-int8 + Redwood-runtime quant profile Q2 (details in quant_profile_recommendation.xlsx).
3) Measurement approach: we’ll instrument token-level counters and track effective per-token cost with/without prefix KV cache. The dev console will show token consumption, cache hit rate, and batching stats.
4) Pricing proposal: pilot credit bucket (30k credits) + overage rate and an optional capped burst at a modest premium. See attached pricing_sheet_v3.csv for numbers.

Next steps: I’ll ask Aditya to outline the quant/batching tradeoffs for your particular trace file and propose a conservative savings estimate (we usually provide a range: baseline, expected, best-case). Marissa will help with commercial terms if procurement wants a short SOW.

Action items:
- Aditya: run the customer traces through the recommended quant profiles and return a short spreadsheet with expected token-savings (ETA EOD 5/18).
- Marissa: draft a 1-page SOW + basic pilot T&Cs for procurement.

Sam — please confirm the procurement contact name and any internal approval thresholds we should watch for.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0123
Attachments: pilot_scope_v2.pdf, pricing_sheet_v3.csv
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@fastops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 17:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot inquiry — efficiency + pricing questions

Neha / Sam — I ran the sample traces Sam attached through two candidate setups and summarized the tradeoffs. Attached is the detailed workbook (quant_profile_recommendation.xlsx). High level: 

- Setup A (Llama-3-70B, int8 + KV-cache enabled, conservative batching): expected token-cost reduction ~22–28% vs your current hosted baseline. Latency impact negligible for median seqs; 95p latency projected ~360ms (slightly above target) but still within acceptable for many flows.
- Setup B (same model with more aggressive 4-bit quant and larger batch windows): expected cost reduction ~36–44% but 95p latency spikes to ~530ms during peak concurrency. Works if your UX can accept occasional slower tails or we implement partial routing to faster variants.

Notes / recommendations:
- Start pilot on Setup A to validate instrumentation; if quality & UX look good after week 2, we can A/B to Setup B for daytime traffic.
- We can enable predictive prefix caching to increase hit rates for repeated query surfaces — I estimate an additional 8–12% saving on top of the above if hit rate >30%.
- Pricing sketch: apply credits to baseline consumption; when using aggressive quant (Setup B) we’d recommend a small uplift on the effective credit burn to account for additional validation support.

I put row-level assumptions in the workbook; Sam, if you can confirm whether peak concurrency might hit 200 users, I’ll re-run the worst-case tail numbers.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Sr. Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: quant_profile_recommendation.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: procurement@blueharbor.com, Sam Lee <sam.lee@fastops.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: SOW + Pilot commercial outline for BlueHarbor (draft)

Hi procurement team — looping in a short pilot SOW and the commercial outline you requested. Key parts here:

- Duration: 6 weeks (start date TBC).
- Credit bucket: 30,000 credits covering baseline consumption on Setup A; overage priced at $0.015/credit up to a capped burst of 10k credits; for aggressive quant flag (Setup B) there is a +12% service uplift.
- Success criteria: measurable >=15% per-token cost reduction and stable UX (no more than 5% requests with latency > 600ms).
- Data security: pilot runs in Redwood Dedicated with optional VPC peering; audit logs are enabled.
- Termination: 7-day notice; data export included.

I attached a one-page SOW template and the pricing sheet. If procurement needs different billing cadence or PO language I can adapt quickly.

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Solutions | Redwood Inference
Attachments: pilot_sow_onepager.docx (attachment stub), pricing_sheet_v3.csv
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@fastops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOW + Pilot commercial outline for BlueHarbor (draft)

Thanks everyone — this is really helpful. Procurement here (procurement@blueharbor.com) has reviewed the one-pager and asked for two small edits:

1) Replace the capped burst clause with an explicit approval flow for bursts > 10k credits (procurement approval required).
2) Add a line that pilot support includes one 2-hour onboarding workshop and weekly 30-min check-ins.

Marissa — can you update the one-pager and send back a redlined version? Aditya — once Marissa confirms, can you re-run the numbers assuming a short daily batch-window at 11am-12pm (we see a 2x spike then) and call out expected tail latency during that window?

If we can get the redline and updated numbers by EOD Thursday 5/20, procurement will sign and issue a PO next week.

Cheers,
Sam
Sam Lee | Director, AI Platforms | FastOps
